title: a `neural_block` descriptor with no `arg_spec` key at all is rejected in BOTH languages, at DIFFERENT stages
why: Fixture content is row01's golden with the `arg_spec` key removed entirely
(not emptied — row01's golden already carries an EMPTY `arg_spec: []`,
which is the REQUIRED shape; this row removes the key).
C++ `parse_sidecar` structurally REQUIRES the `arg_spec` key for every
sidecar, unconditionally (pattern-agnostic, like every other field it
reads) — its absence throws 'sidecar missing arg_spec' at PARSE time,
before `validate_sidecar` (and so the neural clause) ever runs.
Python has no separate parse step, so its `_validate_neural_block`
clause requires the key itself, with the message '... the key is absent'.
This is a companion fact: presence IS
enforceable here — unlike the forbidden-field class H1 rules on — because
C++ structurally requires this particular key at parse for every sidecar,
so there is no in-memory road (door #3/#5) on which the key could be
silently absent without already having failed.
Both drivers' reject-capture already spans parse+validate (the C++ driver
constructs the `Sidecar` via `parse_sidecar` inside the same try that
asserts the substring), so this row exercises different code PATHS in the
two languages while asserting the SAME shared substring ('arg_spec'),
which stops before either language's more specific wording diverges —
the same rendering rule applied to a parse-vs-validate divergence rather
than a set-rendering one.
